parallel.requirements: Recognized the complete Python-Paillier project scope: key generation, encryption/decryption, encoded floats, homomorphic arithmetic, keyring, serialization, CLI, package exports, docs, examples, dependencies, and tests.
parallel.plan_and_ownership: The parent kept final implementation and integration ownership while spawning setup, test, and CLI inspectors to gather reference behavior and packaging details in parallel.
parallel.implementation: The parent imported the upstream phe 1.5.0 source distribution as a baseline, then patched public exports, keyring behavior, serialization helpers, randomness validation, setup metadata, pyproject, docs, examples, and compatibility tests.
parallel.integration_and_delivery: The parent assembled the final workspace as an installable package, added project scaffolding and support files, performed editable install checks, and delivered a coherent final tree.
parallel.verification: The parent ran the upstream 234-test suite before changes, added compatibility tests, ran 238 tests after modifications, installed the package, and reran 238 tests after the final packaging step.
parallel.unfinished_or_incorrect: The prompt-level submit tool was unavailable in the agent environment, but the current official evaluator later completed and passed all 234 tests; no unresolved trajectory-visible parallel defect remains.

serial.requirements: Recognized the same Paillier package scope, including core crypto behavior, exports, keyring/indexing, serialization, CLI, setup.py, docs, examples, and local tests.
serial.plan_and_ownership: A single agent handled inspection, implementation, packaging, local tests, install checks, and final reporting without delegation or subagent handoffs.
serial.implementation: The serial agent directly wrote a standalone implementation and repo scaffold, preserving much upstream behavior but using its own root-level local tests and final project layout.
serial.integration_and_delivery: It added setup.py, pyproject, docs, examples, third-party notices, root tests, and packaging metadata, then verified installability and the console script before finalizing.
serial.verification: It ran the upstream public test files earlier in development and reached 234 public passes, but after adding repo-level scaffolding it only reran 16 local tests plus install, CLI, and star-import checks.
serial.unfinished_or_incorrect: The final serial artifact was near complete but the current official evaluator reports one failed test out of 234; the trajectory does not expose the exact hidden/evaluator edge.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel recognized the full package specification and explicitly aligned root exports, keyring, serialization, CLI, docs, examples, and packaging with the prompt.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial recognized the same broad requirements and implemented the same high-level package, CLI, docs, examples, and export surface.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Requirement recognition was similar; the material difference was not prompt understanding but how each run implemented and verified the final artifact.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel decomposed early into setup, tests, and CLI inspection children while the parent retained implementation and integration ownership.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial used one owner for the entire inspect, implementation, scaffolding, verification, and final response pipeline.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel gained parallel reference discovery while retaining a clear parent integrator; serial avoided coordination overhead but had less simultaneous coverage.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel children received the same prompt context and returned setup/CLI/test findings; the parent could inspect results and continue with its own baseline-driven implementation.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial had no child interface boundary; all context stayed in one agent thread and decisions were local.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel had more handoff surfaces, but no handoff produced stale, missing, or conflicting requirements that affected the delivered artifact.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel extracted the upstream source distribution into the workspace and layered small compatibility and project-scaffolding patches on top.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial wrote the core package and scaffolding directly in a single large patch after inspecting the installed package and reference tests.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel stayed closer to the upstream baseline through final integration, while serial used a bespoke reconstruction that official evaluation later found one edge short.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel received setup and CLI child results, waited/listed active agents, then interrupted a still-running test inspector only after the parent had completed its own verified implementation path.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial had no child result lifecycle; every finding, patch, and final decision stayed in the single thread.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel had redundant child work and a rejected lifecycle near-match, but no needed result was lost or trapped; serial had no analogous coordination boundary.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel final integration was performed by the parent through explicit package, docs, examples, setup, pyproject, and compatibility-test patches followed by full test reruns.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial integrated its root-level package, docs, examples, third-party notes, and local tests in a single-agent workspace and fixed local test harness issues.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel produced a coherent final tree from a baseline package and verified it after integration; serial also integrated cleanly but its final tree still missed one official case.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel ran 234 upstream tests on the baseline, then after API/scaffolding changes and install steps reran the integrated suite to 238 passes before final response.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial ran the upstream public test files earlier, but its final post-scaffolding acceptance was 16 local tests plus install, CLI help, and star-import checks.
comparison_dimensions.difference: This is the clearest process difference for the parallel-only pass: parallel closed with broader integrated verification, while serial closed with a narrower final check and official evaluation found one miss.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel used more time and tokens with four subagents, but it finished normally within the budget, delivered a final response, and official evaluation completed successfully.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial finished faster with no subagents and normal process status, but official evaluation completed with one failed test.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel's extra budget use did not displace necessary work; it bought broader inspection/verification. Serial's shorter path closed before catching the final official edge.

outcome_analysis.explanation: The current completed official records make this a parallel-only pass: parallel passed 234 of 234 and serial passed 233 of 234. The trajectory evidence supports a process-level explanation rather than a precise hidden-test root cause. Parallel imported the upstream source distribution, patched around it, and reran the integrated package suite after final install and packaging changes. Serial also produced a near-complete implementation and ran upstream public tests earlier, but after later scaffolding and test-harness edits it closed on a much smaller local suite and smoke checks. The official one-test serial miss is therefore best explained as an ordinary implementation or final-verification gap in the serial attempt, not as a parallel-side concurrency error.
parallel_contributors: Used the upstream phe source distribution as a behavioral baseline before patching the requested extra API, serialization, keyring, and packaging surface.
Kept parent ownership of final integration and reran the integrated suite after final packaging/install changes.
serial_contributors: Built a standalone implementation that was close enough for 233 of 234 official tests but did not preserve every evaluated edge.
Final closure relied on 16 local tests and smoke checks after broad public-test verification had happened earlier.
ordinary_implementation_differences: The official serial failure is an implementation or verification miss in a single-agent solution; the raw trajectory does not expose the exact failing hidden assertion.
Parallel's baseline-preserving implementation path reduced the chance of divergence from the reference behavior.
outcome_analysis.causal_scope: supported comparative contributors, not an exclusive root cause

The parent owned integration of package exports, keyring, serialization, docs, setup metadata, install checks, and final tests.
The final deliverable was assembled by the parent with setup.py, pyproject.toml, docs, examples, and package files present in the artifact.
The parent controlled the end-to-end path from reference inspection through implementation, install, full test rerun, and final response.
Reference inspection preceded some implementation, but productive work and child inspection overlapped and no mandatory serial gate delayed an unfinished requirement.
Parallel did not complete all investigation as a separate phase before implementation; parent implementation and child inspection proceeded concurrently and finished normally.
No indispensable implementation, integration, or correction path was starved; the parent completed and verified the critical path.
Parallel used several children and more tokens, but finished within budget with full local and official passes; fan-out did not exhaust acceptance work.
The interrupted test child was broad, but the parent did not depend on its unfinished work and no required final behavior was left incomplete by that scope.
No child followed an observably incomplete brief that omitted a known requirement and produced unusable work or an unmet stage.
Children were used for inspection/redundant exploration rather than separately owned components that had to interoperate through omitted contracts.
There is no evidence that known requirements or findings disappeared through transfer and caused repeated work or a wrong action.
Child handoffs were not shown to be too large or too unstructured for parent use; parent completed integration and verification.
No parent action consumed a superseded child report or old workspace state causing rework or invalid verification.
No incompatible child reports or contracts remained unresolved at a decision point; final parent behavior was coherent and verified.
Parallel did not declare completion on only component checks; it ran integrated tests after final packaging/install changes and official evaluation passed.
No replacement child or retry repeated prior work without inherited findings; the trajectory shows continuation, not a checkpoint-free retry failure.
